result.title: Outcome-Aware Agents: When Does Causal Structure Help a Forward Model Foresee the Consequences of Actions?
result.comment: 16 pages, 7 tables. Revised and corrected version of the preprint at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20379456 (withdraws its 36x safety claim). Code and per-seed results: https://github.com/mplusm/AC-LSCM-Outcome-Aware-Research-Paper
result.summary: Agents that act on real systems should predict what their actions will cause before acting. We study when causal structure helps a learned forward model do this, using a planner that rejects candidate actions whose simulated multi-step outcome is unsafe, in synthetic structural causal models where the true consequences are known. We compare the Action-Conditioned Latent Structural Causal Model (AC-LSCM: per-factor mechanisms over a learned sparse graph, actions as do-interventions) with three unstructured forward models on seven random graphs with 10 or 20 variables, a task configured by a fixed rule, and two controls: a do-wrapper that gives every model the same action semantics, and counterfactual data given to all models or to none. When its factors are the observed variables, AC-LSCM recovers the true graph exactly on every 10-variable graph and has lower three-step prediction error than every baseline in all 396 paired comparisons. Its excess safety violations over an oracle are 0.25 of the no-model level on 10-variable graphs (best baseline 0.31) and 0.41 on 20-variable graphs (0.53), and its margin is largest for two-variable actions never seen in training (0.18 versus 0.28). With learned latent factors the same model is worse than the baselines; the choice of factors matters more than the explicit do-operator or counterfactual data, and every planner stays far from the oracle. This version corrects an earlier one, whose model learned an empty graph and whose headline 36x safety improvement came from a task that tested only extrapolation of action values; we withdraw that claim. Code and all per-seed results are released.

AI.brief_summary: 在真实后果已知的合成结构因果模型中，把「以动作为 do-干预、在稀疏学得图上按因子建模」的 Action-Conditioned Latent SCM 前向模型与三种非结构化前向模型对比，考察因果结构何时有助于多步预判动作后果并过滤不安全动作；结论是因子选择比显式 do 算子或反事实数据更关键，而使用学得潜因子时反而不如基线。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「因子化 latent 状态＋稀疏因果图＋动作即干预」的前向建模，可供核查 LVR 推理状态是否会以结构化因子与干预语义组织；「学得潜因子反而变差」的负结果也提示潜空间因子选择与可辨识性可能影响推理期状态的使用效果。
